channel.title: HotNews — China, every day.
channel.description: Daily stories about China in technology, finance, sports, entertainment, lifestyle, science, travel and culture — for readers around the world.

item.title: China's Auto Industry Hits Reset as Deals and Alliances Shift
item.description: From Huawei's promise not to build cars to Porsche's recycled-battery cells and a new Beijing auto show, China's car sector is entering a decisive phase of consolidation, export growth and technological repositioning.

item.title: China's Auto Industry Pivots to Skills as Global Ambitions Grow
item.description: As Chinese automakers expand worldwide, a national skills competition in Shanghai highlights the growing demand for technicians who can build and repair next-generation vehicles. The event showcases how training and industry collaboration are shaping the future of mobility.

item.title: Huawei Repeats 'We Don't Build Cars' as China's Auto Alliances Shift
item.description: Huawei founder Ren Zhengfei told Dongfeng executives the company will keep helping automakers build smarter cars rather than making its own, while Huawei's car chief said the Aito partnership with Seres is being adjusted at Seres' request.

item.title: China's New Family Dramas Ask Who Pays for Love
item.description: Two recent Chinese films, including the September release Burning Dad, are pushing audiences to question the idea that family love must be proven through sacrifice. Critics and viewers say the debate reflects a quiet shift in how Chinese families talk about duty and selfhood.

item.title: China's Micro-Drama Boom: One Family Spent 225,000 Yuan on Short Shows
item.description: A viral Chinese media report tells of a woman in her late sixties who spent 225,800 yuan over two years on micro-dramas — the vertical, minute-long soap operas reshaping Chinese entertainment. The story has sparked a national conversation about binge-watching, auto-renewals and how older viewers get hooked.

item.title: China's Music World Embraces Nostalgia as Liu Huan Dies at 63
item.description: The death of beloved singer Liu Huan at 63 has amplified a wave of nostalgia in China's music scene, where older songs now dominate streaming playlists. A new generation is rediscovering classic hits from the 1980s and 1990s.

item.title: China's Silver Screen Heats Up With Diverse New Releases
item.description: Chinese cinemas are offering a rich mix of domestic dramas, comedies, and international epics this week, from a culinary road trip to a Quentin Tarantino double bill. Audiences can also revisit classics like 'The Shawshank Redemption' on the big screen.

item.title: Apple and Qualcomm Renew Patent Deal, Adding $75 Billion in a Day
item.description: Apple and Qualcomm signed a new global patent licensing agreement effective April 2027, ending years of uncertainty over royalty payments. Apple shares hit a record high, adding roughly $75 billion in market value in a single session.

item.title: Luckin Coffee Lands $1 Billion From Abu Dhabi Fund Mubadala
item.description: Abu Dhabi sovereign fund Mubadala is investing about $1 billion in Luckin Coffee alongside its controlling shareholder, a striking vote of confidence in the chain that once nearly collapsed after a fraud scandal.

item.title: China's A-Share Earnings Rebound Lifts Tech, Resources and Finance Sectors
item.description: Half-year results show Chinese listed companies' profits accelerating in the second quarter of 2026, with semiconductors, metals and brokerages leading gains while consumer names lag. The recovery is spreading across more industries, though the picture remains uneven.

item.title: China's Indie and AAA Studios Bet Big on Global Audiences
item.description: From a top-down extraction shooter to a King Arthur action epic, Chinese developers are pushing ambitious new titles onto Steam and consoles, aiming squarely at players worldwide.

item.title: Chinese Game Studios Bet Big on Global PC and Console Markets
item.description: Several Chinese developers are preparing notable PC releases, including the action RPG Path of Exile 2 approaching 1.0 and the co-op shooter No Such Place set for Steam early access in October.

item.title: Heroes of Might and Magic III Returns: A 27-Year-Old Strategy Classic Gets a 3D Remake
item.description: Ubisoft has announced a full 3D, 4K remake of Heroes of Might and Magic III, the 1999 turn-based strategy game that still holds a devoted global following. It arrives in 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with both original expansions included.

item.title: IKEA's Matter Smart Home Gear Finally Heads to China
item.description: After launching overseas, IKEA's affordable Matter-compatible smart home products are quietly clearing Chinese certification, signaling an imminent mainland debut. The move could shake up a market long dominated by local ecosystems like Xiaomi and Huawei.

item.title: Michelin Guide Debuts in Shenzhen, Awarding Seven Stars at First Judging
item.description: The 2026 Michelin Guide for Guangzhou and Shenzhen marks Shenzhen's first appearance as a Michelin destination, with seven starred restaurants debuting. The combined list features 176 eateries and reflects a dining scene shifting from rapid expansion to operational maturity.

item.title: Why Grown-Ups in China Are Spending Serious Money on LEGO
item.description: Adult LEGO building has become a genuine lifestyle in China, with working professionals buying cars, flowers and World Cup trophies in brick form. Brands and celebrities are now courting this playful, high-spending grown-up audience.

item.title: Why Rubbing a Strand of Hair Curls It Into a Tiny Spring
item.description: A simple kitchen-table experiment reveals a strange fact about human hair: pull a strand between your fingernails and the end coils into a perfect helix. Scientists say the answer lies in how hair is built, not in magic.

item.title: Asian Games: China's Track Stars Shine as Hangzhou Heats Up
item.description: China's sprinters and hurdlers dominated a rain-soaked day at the Asian Games in Hangzhou, while badminton and table tennis players advanced deep into their brackets. The Games, held in the eastern Chinese city, have become a showcase for the host nation's rising sports talent.

item.title: Asian Games Day 3: China's Badminton and Table Tennis Teams Roll On
item.description: At the Hangzhou Asian Games, China's Wang Zhiyi advanced in badminton singles after her Korean opponent retired, while Chinese pairs dominated badminton doubles and table tennis quarterfinals. The men's football team reached the semifinals for the first time since 1998.

item.title: China's Sprinters Storm Into Asian Games Hurdles Final
item.description: Two Chinese hurdlers advanced to the men's 110m final on a rain-soaked night in Hangzhou, while China's badminton and table tennis squads powered deeper into the Asian Games knockout rounds.

item.title: AI Film Studios in China Draw Calls From Cities Eager to Host Them
item.description: Chinese cities and industrial parks are courting AI filmmakers as production costs collapse, with some AI short dramas now costing just a few hundred yuan per minute. Shenzhen-based creator Zhu Zhili says the offers keep coming.

item.title: China's FAST Telescope Rewrites the Story of Why Star-Making Slows
item.description: By pairing the FAST radio telescope with a US dark-energy survey, an international team found that galaxies are not running out of star-forming gas — they are losing the ability to turn it into stars.

item.title: OpenCode Makes DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Credit Permanent
item.description: OpenCode has made its $60 credit for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash permanent, a move that lowers the cost of AI coding for developers worldwide. The promotion, originally temporary, now locks in a key price advantage for the Chinese model.

item.title: Hilton Now Reaches 300 Destinations Across China
item.description: Hilton says its China portfolio has grown past 1,100 hotels spanning 300 destinations, from major cities to smaller county-level towns. The expansion reflects global hotel groups racing to serve China's domestic travelers.

item.title: Banyan Tree Buys African Hotel Group, Expanding to Seven New Countries
item.description: Singapore-based Banyan Tree Group has agreed to acquire a majority stake in Newmark Hotels & Reserves, adding seven African countries to its global portfolio. The deal, announced September 17, marks a major step in the luxury hospitality brand's international expansion.

item.title: Hong Kong's Rosewood Hotel Named World's Best for a Second Year
item.description: The 2026 edition of the world's most-watched hotel ranking, now rebranded simply as The 50, kept Hong Kong's Rosewood at number one. The list and a wave of new China openings show how fast the country's luxury travel map is being redrawn.

item.title: China's Auto Repair Talent Gap Grows as EV Boom Accelerates
item.description: China's electric vehicle boom is creating a shortage of skilled repair technicians, with salaries doubling but positions still unfilled. The WorldSkills competition in Shanghai highlights the advanced skills needed for modern vehicles.

item.title: China's Auto Industry Faces a Wave of New Models and Deals
item.description: A busy week in China's car market brought nine new model launches, a major restructuring between two state-owned automakers, and a shift in the Huawei-Seres partnership, signaling intensifying competition and consolidation.

item.title: China's Electric Car Repair Shops Can't Find Enough Workers
item.description: As electric vehicles flood Chinese roads, repair shops are struggling to hire technicians who understand both mechanics and software. At the WorldSkills competition in Shanghai, young mechanics showed why the job now demands programming skills.

item.title: China's EV Repair Shortage: Double the Pay, Still No Takers
item.description: As electric vehicles flood Chinese roads, a severe shortage of qualified repair technicians is emerging. Fixing an EV now demands mechanical, electrical and software skills — and training pipelines are struggling to keep up.

item.title: One Day, Nine New Cars: Inside China's Crowded EV Market
item.description: On September 23, nine new models from brands like Geely, Changan and Denza hit Chinese showrooms in a single day. The pile-up reflects brutal competition in the world's largest car market, where too many models chase too few buyers.

item.title: Booker Prize 2026 Shortlist Unveiled, Celebrating Writing AI Cannot Copy
item.description: The 2026 Booker Prize shortlist, announced in London, features six novels from four countries, including two past winners and three first-time nominees. Chair of judges Mary Beard calls the list 'literary writing at its best,' highlighting works that resist AI replication.

item.title: China's AI Comic Drama Boom Meets Its First Big Shakeout
item.description: China's AI-generated comic dramas exploded to over 380,000 titles in eight months, but falling platform payouts triggered a 42% studio exit. The crisis echoes Japan's 1980s animation downturn, and creators are hunting for a sustainable model.

item.title: China's Box Office Buzz: Local Heroes and Global Classics
item.description: Chinese cinemas are rolling out a diverse slate this week, from the historical epic 'Dunhuang Heroes' to Quentin Tarantino's 'Kill Bill' re-release, while new comedies and thrillers keep audiences entertained.

item.title: China's Box Office This Week: Auteurs, Blockbusters and One Big Cast Reunion
item.description: Chinese cinemas are juggling a packed slate this week — from a Tang-dynasty epic to Nolan's Odyssey — while Hong Kong veterans Tony Leung Ka-fai and Yu Qian share the screen in a new crime comedy.

item.title: China's Screens Are Full of Stories — And One Big Goodbye
item.description: A beloved Chinese actor, You Benchang, died at 93, while cinemas fill with new releases from mainland China and Hollywood and short-form AI animation floods online platforms.

item.title: China's Sitcom Drought: Why the Laugh Track Fell Silent
item.description: A viral essay asks why China rarely produces hit sitcoms anymore, tracing the genre from 1993's 'I Love My Family' to 'iPartment' — and what streaming, censorship and short video changed.

item.title: China's ETF Market Hits New Milestone as Bond Funds Top $1 Trillion
item.description: China's bond exchange-traded funds have crossed the $1 trillion mark for the first time, while new stock indices launch for innovative drugs and software services. The milestone reflects growing investor appetite for diversified, low-cost investment tools in mainland markets.

item.title: China's A-Shares Add $7 Trillion in Two Years — So Who Actually Won?
item.description: Shanghai's benchmark index has climbed 45% since September 2024, adding roughly 51 trillion yuan in market value. Yet many ordinary investors say they have little to show for the rally, a gap that reveals how unevenly Chinese stock gains are distributed.

item.title: Hong Kong Exchange to Accept Chinese Government Bonds as Collateral
item.description: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing will let traders pledge Chinese government and policy bank bonds held via Bond Connect as collateral from November 2026, deepening the bond market's global role and freeing up capital for derivatives trading.
